signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Geopolitical Blockade
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.50, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster of 160.34/161.09 while remaining above the SMA200 at 158.24. High-impact headlines confirm the U.S. naval blockade of Iran remains in full force, maintaining a geopolitical risk premium that typically supports JPY; however, the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage continues to favor the USD side. Options markets are aggressively hedging for a reversal, with 25d Risk Reversals at -1.96 showing a strong put skew, while the VRP at -1.3% suggests implied volatility is trading below realized levels. Despite the carry cushion, the pair remains highly sensitive to intervention risk as it tests the 160.00 handle, especially with JPY COT Leveraged Funds net short at -59,526 (pctl 73). Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance remains the primary driver while VIX stays at 15.6. Catalyst: Fed Minutes on 19 Aug. BoJ holds at 1.0%.

signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/JPY at 113.29 is the focal point of a bilateral G10 theme as AUD outperformance meets JPY weakness. The pair is supported by a massive +335bp AONIA-TONA carry premium, which represents the highest spread in the G10 cross-selection. While AUD Leveraged Funds are net long +45,727 (pctl 75), the retail community is aggressively fading the move with 91% short, creating a significant institutional-retail divergence. The AUD/USD technical position remains strong above the SMA20/50/200 cluster, suggesting the underlying AUD bid is broad-based. However, the ESI for AUD at -6.3 indicates local data is beginning to miss expectations, which may eventually cap the rally if carry demand cools. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY; carry-driven divergence supported by retail capitulation risk. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep (NZD/AUD proxy). Risk: JPY intervention or sharp equity sell-off compresses the 335bp carry advantage.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Risk
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3546, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster centered near 1.34. COT Leveraged Funds are net long +42,722, which sits at the 90th percentile of its 52-week range, signaling a crowded speculative long. BoE holds at 3.75%. Options pricing reflects this tension, with a significant +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%) indicating high demand for protection against a trend breakdown. Retail sentiment is also extreme at 77% short, which has provided fuel for the trend but now leaves the pair vulnerable to a 'buy the rumor, sell the fact' event. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; crowded positioning and high vol premium limit further upside conviction. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: A break below the SMA20 at 1.3433 triggers a liquidation of spec longs.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5885 is testing the SMA20 at 0.5852 as the RBNZ remains in a hiking cycle (2.5% rate) against a neutral Fed. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This setup creates an asymmetric short-squeeze risk if the RBNZ delivers further tightening or hawkish guidance, as speculators are currently positioned for a dovish pivot that isn't supported by policy. The accommodative real rate of -1.56% in New Zealand further highlights the potential for a hawkish repricing. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze potential against extreme speculative shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep. Risk: RBNZ pauses unexpectedly, validating the crowded speculative short position.
